newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico telephone workers ask Telmex for wage hike.
newsitem.headline: Mexico telephone workers ask Telmex for wage hike.

text.p: Mexican telephone workers have asked Telefonos de Mexico SA (Telmex) for a 47.43 percent wage hike for this year, a union spokesman said on Wednesday.
"We have made a proposal to Telmex, asking for a 47.43 percent wage hike," Enrique Torres, a spokesman for the Mexican Telephone Workers' Union (STRM), told Reuters.
"We expect Telmex will give us an answer on April 4," Torres said.
He said the union planned to meet on April 9 to study the company's counter-offer and warned that if the offer "does not satisfy the workers' interests", the union would call a strike for April 25.
The STRM has some 50,000 members and has in the past avoided calling strikes. In early 1996, it won a 27 percent wage increase from Telmex.
But some workers have complained that inflation has outpaced the wage rise. Consumer prices rose nearly 28 percent in 1996 and 52 percent in 1995. They are seen rising about 17 percent this year.
